tools.name: ssh_exec
tools.description: Run a one-off remote SSH command and return stdout, stderr, and exit metadata. The command runs in a non-interactive context. Use 'cwd' and 'env' for remote directory and environment setup (requires a POSIX shell on the remote). For interactive or long-running commands, use ssh_ensure_session instead.

target.description: OpenSSH target such as host, alias, or user@host.

cwd.description: Remote directory to cd into before running the command.

env.description: Remote environment variables exported before the command runs.

shell.description: Remote shell executable used to wrap the command when shell/cwd/env behavior is needed.

tty.description: Request a remote TTY (ssh -tt). Required for interactive commands (sudo with password prompt, etc.). Avoid for scripted commands: stdout and stderr are merged and ANSI escape codes will be present in output. Default: false.

strict_host_key_checking.description: Boolean or one of yes, no, ask, accept-new, off.

extra_ssh_args.description: Additional ssh(1) flags passed verbatim, e.g. ["-J", "jumphost"]. Prefer the dedicated port, identity_file, and strict_host_key_checking parameters.

tools.name: ssh_scp
tools.description: Copy files or directories between the local machine and one remote target via the local scp client.

target.description: OpenSSH target (host alias or user@host). Specifies the remote host — do not include the host in sources or destination.

sources.description: For upload: local file or directory paths. For download: remote paths (without host prefix — the host is set by 'target').

destination.description: For upload: remote directory path. For download: local directory or file path.

recursive.description: Copy directories recursively. Required when any source is a directory.

strict_host_key_checking.description: Boolean or one of yes, no, ask, accept-new, off.

extra_ssh_args.description: Additional ssh(1) flags passed verbatim, e.g. ["-J", "jumphost"]. Prefer the dedicated port, identity_file, and strict_host_key_checking parameters.

tools.name: ssh_sync
tools.description: Incrementally sync files or directories between the local machine and one remote target via local rsync over SSH.

target.description: OpenSSH target (host alias or user@host). Specifies the remote host — do not include the host in source or destination.

source.description: For upload: local path. For download: remote path (without host prefix).

destination.description: For upload: remote path. For download: local path.

delete.description: Delete files in the destination that are not in the source.

compress.description: Compress data during transfer. Default: true.

dry_run.description: Show what would be transferred without actually doing it.

exclude.description: Glob patterns to exclude from the sync.

strict_host_key_checking.description: Boolean or one of yes, no, ask, accept-new, off.

extra_ssh_args.description: Additional ssh(1) flags passed verbatim, e.g. ["-J", "jumphost"]. Prefer the dedicated port, identity_file, and strict_host_key_checking parameters.

tools.name: ssh_view
tools.description: Read a remote file or list a remote directory over SSH — the remote counterpart of the local file-viewing tool. For a file, returns its content plus 'size_bytes' and 'total_lines'. Content is truncated at 20KB by default when 'view_range' isn't given and 'force_read_large_files' isn't set; use 'view_range' to page through large files instead. For a directory, returns non-hidden entries up to 2 levels deep.

target.description: OpenSSH target such as host, alias, or user@host.

path.description: Absolute (or login-directory-relative) remote path to a file or directory.

view_range.description: Optional [start_line, end_line] (1-based, inclusive). Use end_line -1 for 'to end of file'. Bypasses the 20KB truncation cutoff.

force_read_large_files.description: Read the full file even if it exceeds the truncation cutoff. Ignored when 'view_range' is given. Default: false.

max_bytes.description: Truncation cutoff in bytes for the default (no view_range, no force) read. Default: 20480 (20KB).

strict_host_key_checking.description: Boolean or one of yes, no, ask, accept-new, off.

extra_ssh_args.description: Additional ssh(1) flags passed verbatim, e.g. ["-J", "jumphost"]. Prefer the dedicated port, identity_file, and strict_host_key_checking parameters.

tools.name: ssh_create
tools.description: Create a new remote file over SSH with the given content — the remote counterpart of the local file-creation tool. Fails if the path already exists (use ssh_edit to modify an existing file) or if the remote parent directory doesn't exist.

target.description: OpenSSH target such as host, alias, or user@host.

path.description: Absolute (or login-directory-relative) remote path to create. Must not already exist.

content.description: Full content to write to the new file.

strict_host_key_checking.description: Boolean or one of yes, no, ask, accept-new, off.

extra_ssh_args.description: Additional ssh(1) flags passed verbatim, e.g. ["-J", "jumphost"]. Prefer the dedicated port, identity_file, and strict_host_key_checking parameters.

tools.name: ssh_edit
tools.description: Replace exact text in an existing remote file over SSH — the remote counterpart of the local file-editing tool. Each edit's 'old_str' must match exactly one location in the file (as it stands after any earlier edits in the same call); ambiguous or missing matches fail without writing anything. Provide multiple {old_str, new_str} entries in 'edits' to batch several changes to the same file into a single read-then-write round trip instead of one SSH round trip per edit.

target.description: OpenSSH target such as host, alias, or user@host.

path.description: Absolute (or login-directory-relative) remote path. Must already exist as a regular file.

old_str.description: Exact text to replace; must match exactly one location (include surrounding context to disambiguate).

edits.description: One or more replacements, applied in order against the file's current remote content.

strict_host_key_checking.description: Boolean or one of yes, no, ask, accept-new, off.

extra_ssh_args.description: Additional ssh(1) flags passed verbatim, e.g. ["-J", "jumphost"]. Prefer the dedicated port, identity_file, and strict_host_key_checking parameters.

tools.name: ssh_grep
tools.description: Search remote file contents over SSH — the remote counterpart of the local content-search tool. Backed by remote grep (PCRE-like -P when available, otherwise POSIX extended regex), recursing under 'path' while skipping .git/.hg/.svn. Defaults to 'files_with_matches' mode for efficiency; use 'content' mode for matching lines with line numbers and optional context.

target.description: OpenSSH target such as host, alias, or user@host.

path.description: Remote file or directory to search. Default: '.' (the SSH login directory).

glob.description: Glob filter for which filenames to search, e.g. '*.py' or '*.{ts,tsx}'.

output_mode.description: 'content': matching lines with line numbers (supports context). 'files_with_matches': just the matching paths (default). 'count': per-file match counts (files with zero matches are omitted).

context.description: Lines of context before and after each match. Only applies to output_mode='content'.

context_before.description: Lines of context before each match. Overridden by 'context' if both are given.

context_after.description: Lines of context after each match. Overridden by 'context' if both are given.

head_limit.description: Cap the number of returned matches/files.

strict_host_key_checking.description: Boolean or one of yes, no, ask, accept-new, off.

extra_ssh_args.description: Additional ssh(1) flags passed verbatim, e.g. ["-J", "jumphost"]. Prefer the dedicated port, identity_file, and strict_host_key_checking parameters.

tools.name: ssh_glob
tools.description: Find remote files by name pattern over SSH — the remote counterpart of the local filename-pattern tool. Supports '*', '?', '[seq]'/'[!seq]', '{a,b}' alternation, and '**' for matching across multiple path segments (e.g. 'src/**/*.ts'). A path segment starting with '.' is only matched by a pattern segment that itself starts with '.'. Enumerates under 'path' via remote find, skipping .git/.hg/.svn; matching is done locally.

target.description: OpenSSH target such as host, alias, or user@host.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match, relative to 'path', e.g. '**/*.ts' or '*.{ts,tsx}'.

path.description: Remote base directory to search under. Default: '.' (the SSH login directory).

head_limit.description: Cap the number of returned matches.

strict_host_key_checking.description: Boolean or one of yes, no, ask, accept-new, off.

extra_ssh_args.description: Additional ssh(1) flags passed verbatim, e.g. ["-J", "jumphost"]. Prefer the dedicated port, identity_file, and strict_host_key_checking parameters.

tools.name: ssh_start_session
tools.description: Start a new persistent interactive SSH session backed by a local PTY. Returns the session id, initial output, and observer metadata. If 'truncated' is true or 'pending_output_chars' > 0 in the response, call ssh_read_session to retrieve the remaining buffered output. For most agent workflows, prefer ssh_ensure_session instead — it reuses existing sessions and avoids accidental duplicates.

target.description: OpenSSH target such as host, alias, or user@host.

session_name.description: Stable name for this session, used for recovery and reuse across tool calls. Choose a short, descriptive kebab-case name reflecting the task, e.g. 'deploy-staging', 'tail-api-logs', 'debug-worker-3'. This name also appears in tmux session listings for human observers. Strongly recommended for any multi-step workflow.

cwd.description: Remote directory to cd into at session start.

env.description: Remote environment variables to export at session start.

observer_mode.description: Passive observer mode. Defaults to 'tmux' and falls back to transcript-only observation if tmux is unavailable. 'transcript' always records a transcript and returns a local follow command.

auto_close.description: When true, the session is automatically cleaned up after the remote shell or command exits. Use for one-shot long-running commands where you want session-style output streaming but don't need the shell afterwards. Default: false.

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for initial output. Default: 1.0.

strict_host_key_checking.description: Boolean or one of yes, no, ask, accept-new, off.

extra_ssh_args.description: Additional ssh(1) flags passed verbatim, e.g. ["-J", "jumphost"]. Prefer the dedicated port, identity_file, and strict_host_key_checking parameters.

tools.name: ssh_ensure_session
tools.description: Return an existing running SSH session or start a new one. This is the recommended tool for agent workflows — always provide a descriptive session_name so the session can be reliably found across tool calls and conversations. When a session is reused (reused=true in response), the cwd, env, and shell parameters are ignored — they only apply when creating a new session. Check 'created' vs 'reused' in the response to know which happened.

target.description: OpenSSH target such as host, alias, or user@host.

session_name.description: Stable name for this session, used for recovery and reuse across tool calls. Choose a short, descriptive kebab-case name reflecting the task, e.g. 'deploy-staging', 'tail-api-logs', 'debug-worker-3'. This name also appears in tmux session listings for human observers. Strongly recommended for any multi-step workflow.

cwd.description: Remote directory to cd into (only when creating a new session).

env.description: Remote environment variables (only when creating a new session).

shell.description: Remote shell executable (only when creating a new session).

observer_mode.description: Observer mode to ensure on the reused or newly created session. Defaults to 'tmux' and falls back to transcript-only observation if tmux is unavailable.

auto_close.description: When true, the session is automatically cleaned up after the remote shell or command exits. Only applies when creating a new session. Default: false.

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for initial output. Default: 1.0.

strict_host_key_checking.description: Boolean or one of yes, no, ask, accept-new, off.

extra_ssh_args.description: Additional ssh(1) flags passed verbatim, e.g. ["-J", "jumphost"]. Prefer the dedicated port, identity_file, and strict_host_key_checking parameters.

tools.name: ssh_read_session
tools.description: Read unread output from a tracked SSH session. Set wait_seconds (e.g. 1-10) to block until new output arrives; 0 returns immediately with whatever is buffered right now. Default: 1.0. If 'truncated' is true or 'pending_output_chars' > 0, call again to drain remaining output. Check 'running' to know whether the session is still alive.

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for new output. Default: 1.0. Set higher (5-10) for slow commands. Set 0 for instant polling.

tools.name: ssh_write_session
tools.description: Write text or a control sequence to a tracked SSH session PTY. Always terminate commands with a trailing newline (\n) to submit them. Control characters: \u0003 for Ctrl-C, \u0004 for Ctrl-D, \u001a for Ctrl-Z. Use wait_seconds (e.g. 1-5) to receive the command response in the same call. Check 'pending_output_chars' in the response; if non-zero, call ssh_read_session to drain.

input.description: Raw text to write to the session PTY. Include '\n' to press Enter. Control characters work: '\u0003' for Ctrl-C, '\u0004' for Ctrl-D. Text is written exactly as provided.

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for output after writing. Default: 1.0.

tools.name: ssh_stop_session
tools.description: Terminate a tracked SSH session, close any attached tmux observer, and return final unread output plus exit metadata. The transcript file is preserved on disk.

force.description: Send SIGKILL instead of SIGTERM. Default: false.

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for process to exit. Default: 2.0.

tools.name: ssh_list_sessions
tools.description: List tracked SSH sessions with their session_id, session_name, target, state, uptime, and observer details (including tmux_session_name for cross-referencing with tmux ls). Use session_name filter to find a specific named session.

include_exited.description: Include sessions that have exited. Default: true.

tools.name: ssh_forward
tools.description: Start a dedicated SSH port forward (local or remote). This is a separate tool from ssh_exec/ssh_start_session so MCP clients can permission-gate port forwarding independently. Use direction 'local' to make a remote service reachable on a local port, or 'remote' to expose a local service on the remote host.

target.description: OpenSSH target such as host, alias, or user@host.

direction.description: Forward direction. 'local' binds a local port that tunnels to a remote host:port. 'remote' binds a remote port that tunnels back to a local host:port.

remote_host.description: Destination host from the SSH server's perspective.

bind_address.description: Address to bind on. Default: 127.0.0.1. Set to 0.0.0.0 to expose on all interfaces (use with caution).

strict_host_key_checking.description: Boolean or one of yes, no, ask, accept-new, off.

extra_ssh_args.description: Additional ssh(1) flags passed verbatim, e.g. ["-J", "jumphost"]. Prefer the dedicated port, identity_file, and strict_host_key_checking parameters.

tools.name: ssh_list_forwards
tools.description: List tracked SSH port forwards with their forward_id, direction, ports, target, and running status.

include_stopped.description: Include forwards that have exited. Default: false.

tools.name: ssh_stop_forward
tools.description: Stop a tracked SSH port forward and return its final status.

forward_id.description: ID of the forward to stop.
